strongest_angle: The U.S. Army released an investigation report in October 2026 detailing systemic safety failures and procedural breakdowns behind the January 29, 2025 midair collision involving a Black Hawk helicopter and a civilian jet near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, which resulted in 67 fatalities.

key_facts.fact: On January 29, 2025, a midair collision occurred near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport involving a UH-60L Black Hawk helicopter and a PSA Airlines CRJ700 flight, resulting in 67 deaths according to POLITICO.
The U.S. Army administrative investigation report, appointed by LTG Laura Potter and completed in May, was released publicly on October 8, 2026, revealing systemic safety breakdowns.
The Associated Press reported that the investigation into the January 29, 2025 DCA midair collision was released after months of pressure from victims' families.

The Washington Post noted that the Army report concluded the FAA's route-crossing of military helicopters and civilian jets was a primary factor in the collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.
